newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says Japan watching forex moves closely.
newsitem.headline: MOF says Japan watching forex moves closely.

text.p: Japan is closely watching movements in the currency market and will take appropriate measures towards any excessive moves, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Wednesday.
Asked whether he believed the yen had weakened too much, Mitsuzuka said: "Stability in exchange rates is important. Neither an excessive yen weakening nor a strengthening is desirable," he said.
On the issue of intervention, he merely said: "Calling for stable currencies could lead to stability itself."
He also added that the Group of Seven (G7) industralised nations are keeping in constant touch with each other to cooperate for the sake of the global economy.

The dollar surged to 122.75 yen, its highest level since February 1993, in Tokyo trading on Wednesday, backed by healthy economic fundamentals in the United States and the market's conviction that major nations will tolerate its rise.
